sessionTitle: AI solutions built to power industrial innovation and sovereign control

announcements.name: Foundry Local on Azure Local in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: Foundry Local now runs on Azure Local infrastructure for both connected and disconnected, single-node and multi-node scenarios across Azure Local form factors
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced in public preview Foundry Local running on Azure Local infrastructure, supporting both connected and disconnected scenarios across single-node and multi-node deployments and the different form factors of Azure Local. Models are cached locally and inference runs without any cloud dependency, while operations teams retain full control. Security and governance use the same identity layer as the cloud estate, with identity handled through Microsoft Entra ID and JWT validation, and inference endpoints secured with TLS and API key or token-based authentication. Azure Local is positioned as an AI-ready platform bringing Foundry capabilities to the enterprise edge with pre-validated hardware and Kubernetes-native operation.

announcements.name: Multi-node model catalog and inferencing
announcements.shortDescription: Building on the February single-node ONNX catalog, customers can now run the Foundry Local model catalog and inferencing across multi-node deployments
announcements.longDescription: Building on the February announcement of the Foundry Local model catalog on single-node deployment (suited for customers with ONNX inferencing needs where a single node is sufficient), Microsoft announced that customers who need to scale can now run the Foundry Local model catalog and inferencing capabilities across multi-node deployments. This runs on an Arc-enabled Kubernetes environment across the different form factors of Azure Local, from single-node to multi-node deployment.

announcements.name: Custom and out-of-the-box MCP tools
announcements.shortDescription: Developers can connect custom MCPs or use catalog MCPs to link local data sources alongside chosen models and RAG
announcements.longDescription: As part of the Foundry Local tools capability, developers can connect a custom MCP to their local data sources, combining the right model chosen via RAG capabilities with custom MCPs and other local tools. This combination runs on an Arc-enabled Kubernetes environment across the different form factors of Azure Local, from single-node to multi-node. The platform also allows discovering and deploying curated catalog models or bringing your own model (for example a container with models from Hugging Face such as YOLO 10 [inferred] or other predictive or generative AI), merged with your own OCI registry and served via vLLM or ONNX Runtime.
